lines.t: Like an apple tree among the trees of the woods, So is my beloved among the sons. I sat down in his shade with great delight, And his fruit was sweet to my taste. The voice of my beloved! Behold, he comes Leaping upon the mountains, skipping upon the hills.

My beloved is mine, and I am his; He is the chief among ten thousand. His left hand is under my head, And his right hand embraces me. Sustain me with cakes of raisins, refresh me with apples, For I am lovesick.

Tell me, O you whom I love, Where you feed your flock, where you make it rest at noon. By night on my bed I sought the one I love; I sought him, but I did not find him. “I will rise now,” I said, “And go about the city; In the streets and in the squares, I will seek the one I love.” I sought him, but I did not find him.

My beloved is mine, and I am his; He is the chief among ten thousand. His left hand is under my head, And his right hand embraces me. Sustain me with cakes of raisins, refresh me with apples, For I am lovesick.
Set me as a seal upon your heart, As a seal upon your arm; For love is as strong as death, Jealousy as cruel as the grave; Its flashes are flashes of fire, A most vehement flame.
Many waters cannot quench love, Nor can the floods drown it. My beloved is mine, and I am his.
